text:
Marco Kasper has played four games this season, because an injury in the preseason cost him the first month. He's back now, and an NHL.com headline on Nov. 14 carried the line "He looks confident and strong right now." He scored his first goal of the season in his second game back, in the 5-4 loss in Florida.

Four games tell you very little, but the early shape is encouraging: Detroit has controlled about 58% of shot attempts and 63% of the expected goals with him on the ice at five on five, and he's playing close to 15 minutes. The Hockey News has framed this as a crucial contract year for the 2022 eighth overall pick, coming off a second season that disappointed.

What he brings is position more than power. His shot speed sits near the bottom of the league, but Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 80th percentile last season for chances from the slot in front of the net. With Detroit short down the middle, the question is how much room the team gives him to grow back into a bigger role.
